pageTitle: Using service-linked roles for Directory Service
whatThePageStates: This is the standard AWS service-linked-role (SLR) page for AWS Directory Service. Four of its five sections are pure prose walkthroughs: what an SLR is, the permissions held by AWSServiceRoleForDirectoryService (trusted principal ds.amazonaws.com plus an ec2/ssm action list from AWSDirectoryServiceServiceRolePolicy), how the role is created automatically, that it cannot be edited, and how to delete it. Only the final section, 'Supported Regions for Directory Service service-linked roles', makes a coverage statement: it says Directory Service does not use the SLR in every Region where the service is available, and that the role is used only in Regions where you can opt in to hybrid directories. A single table titled 'Hybrid directory opt-in Region support' then lists 27 Regions (Region name, Region identity, opt-in support), every one marked Yes. No Region is listed as unsupported anywhere on the page.

features.featureName: Hybrid directory opt-in Region support (Regions where the AWSServiceRoleForDirectoryService service-linked role is used)
features.statuses: 27 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial; 27+0+0=27. The 'opt-in support' column holds the literal string 'Yes' in all 27 rows. There is no No, no Partial, no dash, no footnote marker. The table is a pure allowlist: it enumerates only Regions that DO support the capability. The prose sentence 'Directory Service does not support using service-linked roles in every Region where the service is available' asserts that some non-listed Regions exist, but it names none of them, so the page states zero negative values. Any 'No' count from this page is fabricated.
features.scope: None. There is a single global claim about one named role (AWSServiceRoleForDirectoryService) in one service. No per-directory-type, per-edition (AWS Managed Microsoft AD vs AD Connector vs Simple AD), per-partition or per-account-type breakdown is given, even though Directory Service has several directory types. The table has exactly one status column; there is no second dimension to cross with Region.
features.reasoning: The enumerated thing is an AWS Region, one of the external universes in the vocabulary, and each row's unit of claim is 'in this Region you can opt in to hybrid directories, and therefore the SLR is used here'. Region name and Region identity are two labels for the same Region, not two axis values, so the row count and the distinct-Region count are both 27 — the rows do not collapse. The capability being scoped is the SLR / hybrid-directory opt-in, not Directory Service availability as a whole: the page explicitly says the SLR Region list is a subset of the Regions where the service is available.

shouldNotExtract: The role's permissions policy listing is not coverage: the two service prefixes (ec2, ssm) and the 12 IAM action bullets under them (7 ec2:Describe* plus 5 ssm:*) describe what the role is allowed to do, not what Directory Service supports — they are an IAM policy summary, and the page even points to the AWS Managed Policy Reference for the authoritative version. Also not coverage: the single trusted-principal bullet 'ds.amazonaws.com'; the five-item 'Topics' navigation list at the top; the four procedural section headings (Creating / Editing / Deleting / permissions); the Important callout about the role appearing in accounts and the January 1, 2017 date; the Note about deletion failing while the role is in use; the 'To delete Directory Service resources' single-bullet procedure; the eight or so cross-links to the IAM User Guide, the managed-policy reference and ms_ad_delete.md; the column headers 'Region name / Region identity / opt-in support'; and the trailing 'See also — Skills for AI coding assistants' boilerplate with its aws agent-toolkit search-skills command, which is generic AWS site furniture and carries no coverage data.
coverageDimensions: REGION: this is the only dimension the page supplies — 27 named Regions, each affirmatively supported, and nothing else. The universe of AWS Regions is far larger than 27, so unsupported Regions exist by implication but are never named; the page gives a supported list, not a matrix. SERVICE: nothing usable. The page is about exactly one service (AWS Directory Service) and mentions ec2 and ssm only as the targets of IAM actions the role holds; treating those as 'services covered' is wrong. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing. No resource types are enumerated at all — the only resource-ish nouns (VPCs, subnets, security groups, network interfaces, directories, domain controllers) appear inside a prose description of why the ec2:Describe* permissions exist, and inside a delete-your-directory pointer. Any per-service or per-resource-type figure attributed to this page is fabricated.
trap: The biggest trap is inventing a denominator: reading the sentence 'Directory Service does not support using service-linked roles in every Region where the service is available' as a licence to compute 27-of-N and emit N-27 'No' values against some external Region list. The page names no unsupported Region, so the only defensible extraction is 27 Yes and nothing else. Runners-up: (1) harvesting the 12 IAM action bullets or the 2 service prefixes (ec2, ssm) as an apiOperation or service coverage axis — that is a permissions policy, not a support matrix; (2) double-counting each Region because it appears twice per row as a friendly name and as a Region identity, yielding 54; (3) mis-scoping the table as 'Regions where AWS Directory Service is available' or 'Regions where AWS Managed Microsoft AD is available' when it is specifically the hybrid-directory opt-in / SLR list, a strict subset; (4) counting the five 'Topics' bullets or the four how-to sections as features; (5) scraping the 'See also' AI-coding-assistant block as content.
